instructions: 1 to 4 hours ahead: squeeze the orange and 2 of the limes. That should be about 1/3 cup orange juice and 3 tbsp lime juice. Mince the 3 garlic cloves.

In a large bowl, whisk the juices and garlic with 2 tbsp of the oil, the 2 tsp achiote powder, the 3/4 tsp cumin, 3/4 tsp coriander, 3/4 tsp oregano, 1 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Add the 2 lbs chicken and turn it until every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for 1 to 4 hours. Any longer and the citrus makes the chicken mealy.
Take the chicken out of the fridge 15 minutes before you cook. Meanwhile, finely chop the onion, chop 1/2 cup of the cilantro and cut the last lime into wedges.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large cast iron skillet or grill pan over medium high until it shimmers. Lift half the thighs out of the marinade, let the extra drip off and lay them in the pan, smooth side down.

Cook them for 5 to 6 minutes without moving them, until the underside is charred in spots and lets go of the pan. Flip them and cook the other side for 4 to 5 minutes. You're cooking them to 175°F in the thickest part, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest one. It's done when there's no pink left and the juices run clear.
Move them to a board. If the bits in the pan are burning, wipe it out. Add the last 1 tbsp oil and cook the second batch the same way. Throw away the leftover marinade.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, warm the 12 tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat, about 30 seconds a side, and stack them in a clean kitchen towel.
Taste a piece. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lime.
Serve with the warm tortillas, the onion, the cilantro, the lime wedges and the salsa.
advance_prep_notes: marinate the chicken 1 to 4 hours ahead
method_notes: All three versions marinate chicken in orange and lime juice with garlic, achiote, cumin and oregano, then grill it hot until charred and rest it before slicing, with tortillas, onion, cilantro, lime and salsa alongside. Lemon Blossoms adds coriander and caps the marinade at 4 hours, Jo Cooks blends the marinade and takes thighs to 175°F, and That's Deelicious uses pounded breasts and a 1 to 4 hour marinade. This follows the lead's marinade, scaled from 3 lbs to 2 lbs of boneless thighs, and cooks them in a cast iron skillet or grill pan rather than on an outdoor grill, which Jo Cooks also gives as an option.
